history.change: created while fixing review cluster A2, second pass (G00 residuals)

title: Design an out-of-band permit approval an agent process cannot synthesise (a pty with a clean environment passes the tty check)
impact: An agent that allocates a pty, clears CLAUDE*/AI_AGENT variables and detaches from its parent (double fork, reparented to launchd) satisfies is_human_tty, runs `jade permit approve`, and the ledger then holds a forged `human:` principal and `tty:` reference. Cluster B added the ancestor-process check, dropped -y for high/critical, a typed code and wider SI-09 spellings; none of them is a boundary against a same-user process that runs arbitrary code
rationale: The approval and the agent run as one OS user, so any in-band signal (tty, environment, process tree, a typed code readable from the pty master) can be reproduced. A real boundary needs something the agent cannot read or drive
next_action: Choose and prototype one: (a) approval through a macOS Keychain or Touch ID prompt (a small LocalAuthentication helper) that signs the permit fields with a key the agent cannot read, verified by the hook at consume time; (b) a separate OS user that owns the ledger and the approve command (sudo -u with a password prompt on /dev/tty); (c) a signed approval from a second device. Unsigned rows then never cover high or critical commands
retry_or_revisit_trigger: before JADE is run in bypassPermissions/auto or unattended modes, or on the first would_block event that shows an agent-run approve attempt

history.change: created while fixing review cluster B (F06, F07)

title: Bind the content of a Write/Edit/MCP call to its permit, not only the target path
impact: The plan hash of a Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit call covers the target path only (policy._assess_write), so a human who approves a write to a protected file approves any content the agent sends to that path within 30 minutes, and the approval screen cannot show the content
rationale: The permit for a Bash command hashes the whole command text; file content was left out of the hash when only classification by path was designed. Content is already read at the gate by SI-02 and SI-05
next_action: Add a `file_sha` precondition (sha256 of the new content, or of old_string plus new_string for Edit) recorded at request time and compared at consume time, show the content length and a bounded preview on the approval screen, and refuse approval when the content is too large to review

history.change: created while fixing review cluster B (F11, adjacent finding)

title: Capture real hook payloads, close the loop for Write/MCP calls, and decide how a permit survives a parallel hook or a host prompt that denies the call
impact: (1) Permits are bound to session_id and agent_id, but those fields were taken from the host's documentation and tests use synthetic payloads. (2) PostToolUse is installed for Bash only, so a permitted Write/Edit/MCP call stays EXECUTING until its deadline, becomes OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is then held by SI-07. (3) PreToolUse hooks run in parallel and a permit consumed by JADE is not returned when another hook or the host prompt then denies the call, so the retry needs a new permit

history.change: created while fixing review cluster B (G08)

title: The permit seal key is a same-user file: move it where an agent process cannot read it, and close the run-time-built SI-09 routes
impact: Permit rows carry an HMAC seal (permit-seal.key in the JADE home, mode 600). A row edited with SQL is refused at use, but a process that reads the key (a script the agent wrote first; SI-10 only blocks command text that names the file) can re-seal a forged row, and one that double-forks under a pty can approve for real (W-38). SI-09 does not see a command built at run time: importlib.import_module('ja'+'de.permits'), base64 -d | sh, a variable assigned in one command and used in another
rationale: The agent and the human are one OS user, so a key file that user can read is only a speed bump; the seal still turns a naive row edit and a replayed consumed permit into a refusal and gives W-38 a place to plug a real signature
next_action: With W-38: sign the seal in a Keychain item that needs user presence (or a helper run as another user) so the hook can verify and no agent process can produce it; until then decide whether a decode-and-execute pipeline (base64 -d | sh, python -c with importlib and string concatenation) gets its own gated rule in policies/risk.yaml

history.change: created while fixing review cluster B, second pass (F06, F07)

title: Redaction recognises shapes and key names only: a secret with neither still reaches the provider payload and the ledger
impact: redact() and residual() match known vendor prefixes, known key names (password, token, secret, api key, pass, pwd, cookie ...), URL userinfo, Authorization and Cookie headers, curl -u, mysql -p, --password style flags and the line after 'security find-generic-password -w'. A bare high-entropy string with no prefix (a 64-digit hex key, a base64 blob, a Twilio account sid), a secret under an unlisted name (key=, pin=, auth=), one split by a zero-width character, a newline or full-width letters, a password containing a comma after '=', and a secret printed on a line with no command above it all pass unchanged and residual() does not catch them (residual is the union of the high-confidence prefix patterns, not an entropy check).
rationale: A shape and name list cannot be complete; an entropy detector would redact hashes, commit ids and UUIDs that Jev needs as evidence, which is the over-redaction F23 removed. The honest control is that the agent is told not to paste credentials and the ledger is local, mode 600 and purged.
next_action: Measure on the real evidence the agent sends (evals/baseline dataset): count 40-plus character hex and base64 runs outside git ids, decide on an opt-in entropy pass for runs next to a key-like word, and normalise Unicode (NFKC, drop zero-width characters) before matching without changing the text that is stored
retry_or_revisit_trigger: after the next baseline transcript mining run

history.change: created while fixing review cluster C (F14, F17-F23)

title: A gated command that carries an inline secret cannot be approved: add an out-of-band way to review it without storing the secret
impact: Since the redaction fix (F14, F18) a gated command is stored redacted. A human cannot verify what the plan hash covers from a redacted text, so permits.approve refuses and the agent is told to move the secret into an environment variable or a file. A legitimate gated command that must carry a literal credential (a one-off docker login -p, a curl with a bearer token to a production endpoint) is therefore never approvable, and a false positive of the redaction patterns on a gated command has the same effect.
rationale: Showing the secret on the approval screen means storing it; hiding it means approving text the human cannot read. Refusing is the safe choice and costs one retry by the agent in the common case. A better design keeps the secret in the hook process only (a sealed, short-lived entry in a Keychain item the human unlocks) and shows the redacted text plus the digest of the redacted parts.
next_action: Count how often the block message for a redacted command fires in the ledger events (guard text); if it is more than a few a month, design the Keychain-held reveal together with W-38 (out-of-band approval)
retry_or_revisit_trigger: with W-38 or when the block fires repeatedly for one pattern

history.change: created while fixing review cluster C (F14, F17-F23)

title: Promotion has evaluators for two targets only, and only one canary rollback trigger is evaluated
impact: improve.promote derives its results for calibration_threshold and question_template. cache_ttl (auto-promotable by policy), routing_heuristic, escalation_heuristic, state_selection, batch_strategy, skill_reference and performance have no evaluator, so they cannot be promoted by code (a human applies them by hand). Of the canary rollback triggers in policies/promotion.yaml only provider_error_rate is evaluated; false_accept_rate > champion + 0.03 and a resolved model that differs from the candidate's dataset model are not. The evidence the gate reads sits in the ledger, which the same OS user can edit.
rationale: Computing a result needs a replayable, labeled signal per target; none exists yet for the others, and a flag in their place is what the review found. Failing closed costs a manual step; guessing a result costs a bad promotion.
next_action: When a second target is worth improving, write its evaluator (replay on the ledger, paired metrics, protected check) and add its stage to the audit verdict; evaluate the two remaining canary triggers from the ledger rows of the canary sessions; consider sealing the evidence like permit rows (W-41)
retry_or_revisit_trigger: a candidate for a target other than threshold or template, or the first canary

history.change: created while fixing review cluster D (F25, F45)

title: The 20 s provider deadline does not cover DNS resolution or a stalled TCP connect
impact: adapter.http_transport shuts the socket at the deadline with a timer and reads the body against it, which bounds slow headers and a slow body. getaddrinfo and the connect before the first byte are bounded only by the socket timeout (the remaining time), so a resolver that hangs can hold a call past the deadline; the PreToolUse hook never calls the provider, only jade ask and the Stop-path tools do.
rationale: Python gives no portable way to interrupt getaddrinfo; a worker thread leaks the blocked thread. The hook is not exposed, the agent-facing call is, and a stuck resolver is rare.
next_action: If a hang is seen in the ledger (latency_ms above 20000, error_kind UNAVAILABLE), resolve the host once with a deadline in a thread and connect by address, or run the exchange in a subprocess with a kill
retry_or_revisit_trigger: a provider call longer than the deadline in the ledger

history.change: created while fixing review cluster D (F25, F45)

title: Gate environment overrides in the host's own environment are reported and journaled, not ignored
impact: The hook reads JADE_POLICY_DIR, JADE_CONFIG, JADE_HOME and JADE_GATE_MODE from the environment the host gives it. An agent cannot set those for the host's hook processes from a command (SI-11 blocks the spelling, R-13 gates the settings files), but a shell profile, launchctl setenv, a LaunchAgent plist or a project env file edited by a route the classifier cannot read still reaches every later hook. title: Know the limits of reading interpreter programs by what they do
impact: jade/interp.py follows literal commands and write targets. Not seen: a path or command built from input (base64, hex, `importlib`, a stdin read), a file or network read at run time, a command written to a file and run later, a program fed from a script file (`python3 build.py`), a callback table, `eval` of a built string. A dynamic target is not seen: the program is rated by its other literal effects, low when it has none (awk is the exception: an unreadable target makes the whole program count). Seen since the second pass: shlex.split and str.split of a constant, a program whose output is piped into a shell, awk -f from stdin, a command passed as a value (atexit, partial, map, Thread, executors, ctypes), values held in a dict, class attribute, self.x or os.environ, comprehensions over literal lists, os.chdir and cwd=
rationale: A literal reader cannot know what a variable holds; a program that hides its target from a reader is also hiding it from the human who reads the command
next_action: Add a fixture per limit to evals/adversarial as a documented residual, and decide whether a program that runs a shell it built from input should rate high on its own
